methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Lab 91 is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private and public players in Chips & Semiconductors, including public benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and private peers such as Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using the $10M total raised as a proxy for current asset base and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression, this method implies a valuation of $25M. A Peer-Median approach was not viable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Chips & Semiconductors sector; only one adjacent-stage peer was identified in the narrow filter, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. The primary limitation is reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than market multiples or transaction data from true peers. Key unknowns include Lab 91's specific technical differentiation within semiconductors, capital efficiency relative to the comp set, and path to Series A fundraising. A peer-median approach would strengthen conviction once the company reaches scale or additional Seed-stage semiconductor investments enter the dataset.
